# Coloring and Selectors

::: {.callout-important}
## Read this before you write any `.color(...)` or `.component({ selector })` call

The MVS API is strictly schema-validated. Two specific mistakes trip up LLMs and humans alike:

1. Treating `"helix"`, `"sheet"`, `"coil"` as **component selectors**. They are not.
2. Treating `"element-symbol"`, `"by-element"`, `"chain-id"` as **color values**. They are not.

This page documents the exact, exhaustive list of what works.
:::

## The component selector enum is exhaustive

`selector` accepts **exactly one of these nine strings** (the `ComponentSelectorT` type):

```text
'all' | 'polymer' | 'protein' | 'nucleic' | 'branched'
      | 'ligand'  | 'ion'     | 'water'   | 'coarse'
```

Anything else — `'helix'`, `'sheet'`, `'binding_site'`, `'active_site'`, `'chain_A'`, `'residues_5_to_20'` — **will fail validation**. There are no aliases, no synonyms, no case-insensitive matching.

If you need finer slicing, the `selector` parameter also accepts a **ComponentExpression** (or array of them) — a structured object pointing at specific atoms / residues / chains:

```js
// Color residues 5..20 of chain A
structure
  .component({ selector: 'protein' })
  .representation({ type: 'cartoon' })
  .color({
    selector: { auth_asym_id: 'A', beg_auth_seq_id: 5, end_auth_seq_id: 20 },
    color: '#e74c3c',
  });
```

The full set of fields a ComponentExpression accepts:

```text
label_entity_id, label_asym_id, auth_asym_id,
label_seq_id, auth_seq_id, pdbx_PDB_ins_code,
beg_label_seq_id, end_label_seq_id, beg_auth_seq_id, end_auth_seq_id,
label_comp_id, auth_comp_id, residue_index,
label_atom_id, auth_atom_id, type_symbol,
atom_id, atom_index, instance_id
```

`type_symbol` is the element name (e.g. `'C'`, `'N'`, `'O'`); useful for "color all carbons" without invoking a palette.

## Coloring options

### 1. Fixed color (named or hex)

```js
representation.color({ color: 'green' });
representation.color({ color: '#cc3399' });
representation.color({ color: 'orange', selector: 'ligand' });
```

Named CSS colors and `#RRGGBB` strings work. **`'element-symbol'`, `'by-element'`, `'by-chain'` do not** — they look like CSS values but aren't.

### 2. Slice + color (the secondary-structure pattern)

For secondary structure, B-factor regions, or any per-residue/per-chain palette you can enumerate, define ComponentExpression slices and call `.color(...)` once per slice:

```js
const helices = [
  { auth_asym_id: 'A', beg_auth_seq_id: 12, end_auth_seq_id: 24 },
  { auth_asym_id: 'A', beg_auth_seq_id: 56, end_auth_seq_id: 71 },
];
const sheets = [
  { auth_asym_id: 'A', beg_auth_seq_id: 30, end_auth_seq_id: 38 },
];

structure
  .component({ selector: 'protein' })
  .representation({ type: 'cartoon' })
  .color({ color: '#bdc3c7' })                  // default for the rest
  .color({ selector: helices, color: '#e74c3c' })
  .color({ selector: sheets,  color: '#f1c40f' });
```

Notice the pattern: a default `.color(...)` first, then per-region overrides. The order matters; later calls win.

### 3. Color from the same file (`colorFromSource`)

If the structure was loaded from an mmCIF/BinaryCIF that already contains an annotation column (DSSP secondary structure, pLDDT scores, custom labels), point `colorFromSource` at it:

```js
const struct = builder
  .download({ url: '...some_with_annotation.cif' })
  .parse({ format: 'mmcif' })
  .modelStructure({});

struct
  .component({ selector: 'polymer' })
  .representation({ type: 'cartoon' })
  .colorFromSource({
    schema: 'residue',
    category_name: 'pdbx_struct_conf',  // CIF category to read
    field_name: 'conf_type_id',         // column with the value
  });
```

Valid `schema` values are exactly:

```text
'whole_structure' | 'entity' | 'chain' | 'auth_chain'
                  | 'residue' | 'auth_residue'
                  | 'residue_range' | 'auth_residue_range'
                  | 'atom' | 'auth_atom' | 'all_atomic'
```

### 4. Color from an external annotation file (`colorFromUri`)

Same shape as `colorFromSource` but reads from a separate URL — useful when the structure file doesn't include the annotation:

```js
struct
  .component({ selector: 'polymer' })
  .representation({ type: 'cartoon' })
  .colorFromUri({
    uri: 'https://example.org/my_annotation.json',
    schema: 'residue',
  });
```

## Common asks and the right way to do them

| You want… | Wrong | Right |
|---|---|---|
| Color polymer by element | `.color({ color: 'element-symbol' })` | Use `ball_and_stick` representation; molstar's default is element-coloring. For a custom palette, use a ComponentExpression with `type_symbol` slices. |
| Color helices red, sheets yellow | `.color({ selector: 'helix', color: 'red' })` | Either define helix ComponentExpressions yourself (see pattern #2) or load a structure with DSSP annotation and use `colorFromSource`. |
| Color by chain | `.color({ color: 'by-chain' })` | One `.color({selector: {auth_asym_id: 'A'}, color: '...'})` call per chain, or `colorFromSource` with `schema: 'auth_chain'`. |
| Color by pLDDT | `.color({ color: 'plddt' })` | `colorFromSource({ schema: 'residue', field_name: 'pLDDT', palette: {...} })` on an AlphaFold mmCIF. |
| Highlight binding site | `.component({ selector: 'binding_site' })` | `.component({ selector: <ComponentExpression with residue list> })`. |

## Validation safety net

Every value above is checked at scene-evaluation time. Use `scene_validate` (MCP tool) or the editor's Apply button to catch a wrong enum or misspelled key — the error messages enumerate the valid alternatives.
